clue.text: What brings word of source of avian flu?

definitions.text: What brings word of source of avian flu?

parts.words: What brings word of source of avian flu?
parts.note: a bird that delivers messages, read as a bird that carries a disease to other birds

explanation.surface: A question about what spreads news of where bird flu began.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brings word' is the messenger sense; 'source of avian flu' plays on 'carrier', a creature that passes on an infection.
explanation.definitionFit: Homing birds were long used to fly written messages back to their lofts, and a bird bearing a virus is likewise its carrier.

clue.text: Could this represent dicer's luck at all? Almost entirely!

definitions.text: Could this represent dicer's luck at all? Almost entirely!

indicators.note: asks whether the following letters could be rearranged to stand for something else, an anagram signal

parts.note: the possessive s counts as a letter here
taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: almost all of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written before trimming

explanation.surface: A gambler wonders whether chance is really behind their dice, and answers nearly yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost entirely' trims ALL to AL; the anagram of DICERSLUCKATAL is signalled by 'Could this represent'. The whole clue also describes the answer, since a gambler at dice takes one.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamble taken after weighing the odds is what a dice player makes each throw, so the whole clue describes it.

clue.text: Rising row about manager's initial scope

indicators.note: the reversed row goes around the letter, so it acts as a container
in a down clue, rising means the word for row is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats

indicators.note: the initial of the word manager is its first letter

explanation.surface: A rising argument about the boss's first remit, or an escalating row over a manager's role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' turns TIER into REIT, and 'about' puts M (the 'initial' of manager) inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A remit is the area of responsibility given to someone, the range or extent of their brief.

clue.text: I will get it with beer and whisky!

definitions.text: I will get it with beer and whisky!

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: read as 'whisked', so the preceding letters are stirred up

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A drinker boasts of getting drunk on beer chased with whisky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whisky' signals the anagram of I, IT, BEER and AND, and the whole clue describes the drinker's resulting state.
explanation.definitionFit: Drinking beer with whisky chasers leaves one drunk, which is the meaning of the answer.

clue.text: Pope's Rome residence incorporates the reverse of such penitence?

indicators.note: the run of letters found is to be read backwards
the words before it contain within them a run of letters, so this signals letters taken from inside the phrase

explanation.surface: A papal residence in Rome somehow holds the opposite of contrition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incorporates' finds ESROMER spanning 'Pope's Rome residence', and 'the reverse of' turns it round. 'such' links the definition to the device that hides it.
explanation.definitionFit: Penitence is deep regret for wrongdoing, and remorse is a direct synonym for it.

clue.text: Local direction indicator?

parts.note: local is the British word for a nearby pub, and the board hung outside one tells you where it is

explanation.surface: A signpost pointing the way around the neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' is British slang for one's regular neighbourhood pub, not an adjective about the area.
explanation.definitionFit: A painted board outside a public house marks it for passers-by, guiding drinkers to their local.

clue.text: Spot limitations of erroneous policy

indicators.note: the limits of each word are its two outermost letters

explanation.surface: Spot the limits of a wrongheaded policy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limitations of' takes the first and last letters of 'erroneous' and 'policy'.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot something is to catch sight of it, and the answer is an old word for exactly that.

clue.text: Angle article brought up about Italy and old people born locally?

indicators.note: the reversed letters go round the two single letters, so they act as a container
in a down clue, brought up means the two words together are read from the bottom upward

parts.note: a slant is an angle or point of view
an is the indefinite article
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: Someone raises the angle that an Italian article treats the old as true locals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' reverses SLANT plus AN to NATNALS, and 'about' wraps it round IO. I is Italy's international vehicle code.
explanation.definitionFit: Nationals are citizens of a country, people who belong to it by birth, which the question mark flags as loose.

clue.text: Railway worker's representative involving me in hierarchy

parts.note: a lineman maintains railway track; the 's is read as 'is'

indicators.note: the representative word takes in the following letters, so this signals a container

parts.note: an agent acts for or represents someone
taken as written

explanation.surface: A railway employee's union rep drags the speaker into a chain of command.
explanation.walkthrough: A lineman is a worker who maintains railway track; 'involving' is the container signal. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Line management is the chain of supervisors each reporting to the one above, a structured ranking of authority.

clue.text: Feller's to move clumsily near, cutting hint of escape

parts.note: to lumber is to move heavily and awkwardly

indicators.note: cutting here means removing the letter from the word for near

parts.note: near is an old word for stingy, as is mean

indicators.note: the hint of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A man moves awkwardly toward something, cutting off a way out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Near' means stingy, i.e. MEAN; 'cutting' drops E (the 'hint of' escape) to leave MAN. The definition 'Feller's' reads as 'feller is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A feller is one who cuts down trees, and a timber worker in the forest does exactly that job.

clue.text: Plump boys, one getting stuck behind sink

indicators.note: the numeral is placed after the word for sink

parts.note: in golf, to sink the ball is to putt it into the hole
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Chubby lads, one of whom has got jammed behind the kitchen sink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting stuck behind' places I after PUTT.
explanation.definitionFit: Putti are the chubby naked infant figures of Renaissance art, cherubs drawn as well-fed little children.

clue.text: No parking for club, say

indicators.note: no parking means the letter for parking is removed from the club

parts.note: a putter is a golf club
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A sign forbidding parking at a club, quoted as an example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No' removes P from PUTTER. 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To say something is to speak it aloud, and the answer is a verb for voicing words.

clue.text: Book disregarded intelligence in cats and dogs?

indicators.note: the letter for book is ignored, so it is removed from the intelligence word

parts.note: brain means intelligence or brainpower

explanation.surface: A book has ignored how clever cats and dogs are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disregarded' removes B from BRAIN. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: It's raining cats and dogs is an idiom for a downpour, so the phrase stands for heavy falling water.

clue.text: Writing other than the leader achieved prominence

indicators.note: everything but the first letter of the writing word is kept

parts.note: prose is ordinary writing

explanation.surface: Writing, unlike the party leader's, became famous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'other than the leader' drops P from PROSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To rise is to climb to eminence; its past tense describes someone who climbed to a notable position.

clue.text: Father on rough sea catching fish's trail

indicators.note: the father and sea letters hold the fish within them

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

indicators.note: a rough sea is churned up, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
a perch is a freshwater fish; the 's reads as 'is'

explanation.surface: Dad out on choppy water lands a fish and follows its wake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rough' makes ASE, the anagram of the sea letters; 'catching' then holds the fish just after the father. In a down clue 'on' means placed above.
explanation.definitionFit: A paper chase is a cross-country game following a trail of scattered paper, so it is literally a trail to pursue.

clue.text: Friend's after turning in a work for Pixar?

indicators.note: the friend word comes after the other letters
the word in is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
a mate is a friend; the 's reads as 'is'

explanation.surface: A friend has come round to taking part in a Pixar film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses the word 'in'; 'after' puts the friend behind it. The 'a' before 'work' supplies the opening letter, so 'work for Pixar?' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Pixar makes cartoon films, so to bring drawings to life on screen is the studio's typical work.

clue.text: Hopes unit is reorganised for it

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are rearranged into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A department's hopes are restructured in a reorganisation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is reorganised' signals the anagram of HOPES UNIT.
explanation.definitionFit: To be for it is British slang for being about to get into trouble, the same as an idiom of being in a mess.

clue.text: A river once more ebbs and falls

indicators.note: ebbing water flows back, so the word goes backwards

parts.note: again means once more

explanation.surface: A river ebbs and falls again, like a tide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ebbs' reverses the word for once more; the river abbreviation and A follow it, in answer order rather than clue order. 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous waterfalls on the US-Canada border take their name from the river, so the falls are the answer by example.

clue.text: Dishes almost complete with apples or pears?

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the word is left off

parts.note: to complete something is to end it
apple and pear are fruit trees, given as examples

explanation.surface: Dishes nearly finished, with fruit to follow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts END to EN; TREES is given by example, hence the question mark. 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Entrées are courses of a meal, served as plated food at table.

clue.text: The rest they use at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Sailors who use the remaining time for something while afloat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' signals the anagram of THEY USE.
explanation.definitionFit: Shut-eye is informal for sleep, a period of rest with closed eyes.

clue.text: Source of bun otherwise served during tea

indicators.note: one word falls within the other, signalling a container

parts.note: cha is slang for tea
else means otherwise

explanation.surface: Where a bun comes from, otherwise eaten at teatime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Source of bun' looks like wordplay for a letter B but is the definition. 'during' is the container signal and 'served' a link. Chelsea is a district of London.
explanation.definitionFit: A Chelsea bun, a sticky currant spiral pastry, is named after the London district where it originated.

clue.text: Island ballad? Line in island poem not half about sun

indicators.note: the line letter goes inside the island word

parts.note: a cay is a small low island or reef

indicators.note: the half word goes around the sun letter
only half of the word poem is kept, its first two letters

explanation.surface: A song from an island, the line of an island poem half missing about the sun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'island' appears twice: the first is part of the definition, the second gives a small Caribbean islet. The question mark marks a ballad of the islands.
explanation.definitionFit: Calypso is a style of song from the Caribbean islands, especially Trinidad, so it is a ballad from an island.

clue.text: Stream with source blocked produces stink

indicators.note: the stream's source is its first letter, which is removed

parts.note: a creek is a small stream

explanation.surface: A dammed stream turns stagnant and starts to smell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with source blocked' removes C from CREEK. 'produces' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To reek is to give off a strong unpleasant smell, so it is a direct synonym of a bad odour.

clue.text: What's chimney having left at the end — coal?

indicators.note: the left letter is moved to the end of the chimney word

parts.note: a flue is a chimney duct

explanation.surface: Asks what a chimney has left in it after the fire — coal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having ... at the end' shifts L in FLUE to the end. The question mark: coal is one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Coal is burned to give heat, so it is an example of combustible material.

clue.text: Offence church found about the limit

indicators.note: the church letters go round the limit word

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
a rim is an edge or limit

explanation.surface: A church discovers a sin that is beyond the pale.
explanation.walkthrough: CE stands for the Church of England. 'found' and 'the' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: An offence is an illegal act, a breach of the law, which is what a crime is.

clue.text: Preparation of vegetables, discarding head and topping

indicators.note: the first letter, the head of the word, is removed

parts.note: dicing is cutting vegetables into small cubes

explanation.surface: Chopping vegetables, throwing away their heads and tops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discarding head' drops D from DICING.
explanation.definitionFit: Icing is the sweet sugar coating spread on a cake, a covering applied on top.

clue.text: A naval group avoiding fighting in prison

indicators.note: the A and the navy letters are kept out of the fighting word

parts.note: carnage is bloodshed and slaughter in fighting
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A naval unit keeps out of the fighting by staying in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'avoiding' removes A and RN (the Royal Navy, Britain's navy) from CARNAGE. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A cage is a barred enclosure, and figuratively a jail or place of confinement.

clue.text: Promotional material sanctions returning car

indicators.note: the letters come back the other way, read in reverse

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement
oks, as a verb, means approves or sanctions

explanation.surface: Advertising material reports sanctions that return a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns ADOKS round.
explanation.definitionFit: Škoda is a Czech carmaker, so its name stands for one of its vehicles.

clue.text: Stress is evident in printing unit appearance

parts.note: an em is a unit of measure in printing

indicators.note: the word is appears inside the other letters

parts.note: a phase is an aspect or appearance, as of the moon
taken as written

explanation.surface: Stress shows up in the look of a print works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evident in' places the word 'is' just before the final letter of the appearance word.
explanation.definitionFit: To stress something is to give it extra weight or importance, a synonym of highlighting.

clue.text: The GI, say, and the silver

definitions.meaning: the letters of the word for eight can be shuffled into t, h, e, g, i, so these are its pieces

explanation.surface: An American soldier and the family silverware.
explanation.walkthrough: THE GI is made of the letters of EIGHT, so it is literally pieces of that word.
explanation.definitionFit: Spanish silver dollars, worth eight reales, were known by this name, famously in pirate tales.
